arxiv-1712-05878.title: An MPI-Based Python Framework for Distributed Training with Keras
arxiv-1712-05878.creator: Dustin Anderson, Jean-Roch Vlimant, Maria SpiropuluCalifornia Institute of Technology, 1200 E. California Blvd, Pasadena, CA 91125
arxiv-1712-05878.description: Abstract We present a lightweight Python framework for distributed training of neural networks on multiple GPUs or CPUs. The framework is built on the popular Keras machine learning library. The Message Passing Interface (MPI) protocol is used to coordinate the training process, and the system is well suited for job submission at supercomputing sites.

arxiv-2109-08746.title: Persistent Homology of Convection Cycles in Network Flows
arxiv-2109-08746.creator: Minh Quang Le, Dane Taylor
arxiv-2109-08746.description: Abstract Convection is a well-studied topic in fluid dynamics, yet it is less understood in the context of networks flows. Here, we incorporate techniques from topological data analysis (namely, persistent homology) to automate the detection and characterization of convective/cyclic/chiral flows over networks, particularly those that arise for irreversible Markov chains (MCs).

arxiv-2402-10781.title: Towards 6G Evolution: Three Enhancements, Three Innovations, and Three Major Challenges Thanks: R. Singh is with the Department of Electronics and Communication Engineering, Dr B. R. Ambedkar National Institute of Technology Jalandhar, India, email: rohits@nitj.ac.in Thanks: A. Kaushik is with the D
arxiv-2402-10781.creator: Rohit Singh, Aryan Kaushik, Wonjae Shin, Marco Di Renzo, Vincenzo Sciancalepore
arxiv-2402-10781.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Rohit Singh, Aryan Kaushik, Wonjae Shin, Marco Di Renzo, Vincenzo Sciancalepore. Over the past few decades, wireless communication has witnessed remarkable growth, experiencing several transformative changes. This article offers a comprehensive overview of wireless communication technologies, from the foundations to the recent wireless advances and future trends. Specifically, we take a neutral look at the state-of-the-art technologies for the fifth generation (5G) and ongoing evolutions towards 6G, while also reviewing the recommendations of the international mobile communication vision for 2030 (IMT-2030).

arxiv-2402-11337.title: Learning by Reconstruction Produces Uninformative Features For Perception
arxiv-2402-11337.creator: Randall Balestriero, Yann LeCun
arxiv-2402-11337.description: Abstract Input space reconstruction is an attractive representation learning paradigm. Despite interpretability of the reconstruction and generation, we identify a misalignment between learning by reconstruction, and learning for perception. We show that the former allocates a model’s capacity towards a subspace of the data explaining the observed variance–a subspace with uninformative features for the latter.

arxiv-2408-02810.title: Scrambling-induced entanglement suppression in noisy quantum circuits
arxiv-2408-02810.creator: Lea Haas, Christian Carisch, Oded Zilberberg
arxiv-2408-02810.description: Abstract Quantum information scrambling is a process happening during thermalization in quantum systems and describes the delocalization of quantum information. It is closely tied to entanglement, a key resource for quantum technologies and an order parameter for quantum many-body phenomena. We investigate the effect of dephasing noise on a multi-qubit teleportation protocol that experimentally validated quantum information scrambling.

arxiv-2412-09407.title: Uncommon Belief in Rationality
arxiv-2412-09407.creator: Qi Shi, Pavel Naumov
arxiv-2412-09407.description: Abstract Common knowledge/belief in rationality is the traditional standard assumption in analysing interaction among agents. This paper proposes a graph-based language for capturing significantly more complicated structures of higher-order beliefs that agents might have about the rationality of the other agents.

arxiv-2503-22191.title: Limiting Disease Spreading in Human Networks
arxiv-2503-22191.creator: Gargi Bakshi, Sujoy Bhore, Suraj Shetiya
arxiv-2503-22191.description: Abstract . The outbreak of a pandemic, such as COVID-19, causes major health crises worldwide. Typical measures to contain the rapid spread usually include effective vaccination and strict interventions (Nature Human Behaviour, 2021). Motivated by such circumstances, we study the problem of limiting the spread of a disease over a social network system.

arxiv-2507-12729.title: Tensor-Tensor Products, Group Representations, and Semidefinite Programming
arxiv-2507-12729.creator: Alex Dunbar ∗,1,2 and Elizabeth Newman †,1,3
arxiv-2507-12729.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Alex Dunbar ∗,1,2 and Elizabeth Newman †,1,3. The ⋆ M \star_{M} -family of tensor-tensor products is a framework which generalizes many properties from linear algebra to third order tensors. Here, we investigate positive semidefiniteness and semidefinite programming under the ⋆ M \star_{M} -product. Critical to our investigation is a connection between the choice of matrix M M in the ⋆ M \star_{M} -product and the representation theory of an underlying group action.

arxiv-2511-18821.title: Off-Equatorial Orbits around Magnetically Charged Black Holes
arxiv-2511-18821.creator: Xilai Li, David E. Kaplan, Loris Del Grosso
arxiv-2511-18821.description: Abstract We present a complete characterization of stable, off-equatorial circular orbits around magnetically charged black holes (MBHs). For a static, spherically symmetric MBH, we derive an exact analytic expression for the orbital latitude θ \theta as a function of radius r r .

arxiv-2512-06032.title: The SAM2-to-SAM3 Gap in the Segment Anything Model Family: Why Prompt-Based Expertise Fails in Concept-Driven Image Segmentation
arxiv-2512-06032.creator: Ranjan Sapkota, Konstantinos I. Roumeliotis, Manoj Karkee
arxiv-2512-06032.description: Abstract This paper investigates the fundamental discontinuity between the latest two Segment Anything Models: SAM2 and SAM3. We explain why the expertise in prompt-based segmentation of SAM2 does not transfer to the multimodal concept-driven paradigm of SAM3. SAM2 operates through spatial prompts points, boxes, and masks yielding purely geometric and temporal segmentation.

pmc-10586273.creator: Aneesa Fatima, Haia Aldosari, M S Al-Buriahi, Maryam Al Huwayz, Z A Alrowaili, Mohammed S Alqahtani, Muhammad Ajmal, Arif Nazir, Munawar Iqbal, Raqiqa Tur Rasool, Sheza Muqaddas, Abid Ali
pmc-10586273.description: One of the most practical and environmentally friendly ways to deal with the energy crises and global warming is to produce hydrogen as clean fuel by splitting water. The central obstacle for electrochemical water splitting is the use of expensive metal-based catalysts.

pmc-11400673.title: Diagnostic value of an interpretable machine learning model based on clinical ultrasound features for follicular thyroid carcinoma
pmc-11400673.creator: Yuxin Zheng, Yajiao Zhang, Kefeng Lu, Jiafeng Wang, Linlin Li, Dong Xu, Junping Liu, Jiangyan Lou
pmc-11400673.description: BackgroundFollicular thyroid carcinoma (FTC) and follicular thyroid adenoma (FTA) present diagnostic challenges due to overlapping clinical and ultrasound features. Improving the diagnosis of FTC can enhance patient prognosis and effectiveness in clinical management. This study seeks to develop a predictive model for FTC based on ultrasound features using machine learning (ML) algorithms and assess its diagnostic effectiveness.

pmc-11612661.title: Commentary on “Factors associated with diabetic foot ulcers and lower limb amputations in type 1 and type 2 diabetes supported by real‐world data from the German/Austrian DPV registry”
pmc-11612661.creator: Mostafa Javanian, Mohammad Barary, Soheil Ebrahimpour
pmc-11612661.description: ed in your esteemed journal. The study provides an essential contribution to understanding the risk factors for diabetic foot ulcers (DFUs) and lower limb amputations, using real‐world data from a significant cohort of adults with type 1 (T1D) and type 2 diabetes (T2D).

pmc-12374306.title: Interleukin-13 gene polymorphisms and asthma susceptibility in children: a meta-analysis
pmc-12374306.creator: Song Su, Tong Zhang, Yaping Wang, Huan Zhang, Meng Wang, Wandong Hu, Ying Ren, Fen Zhao, Hongwei Zhang
pmc-12374306.description: BackgroundInterleukin (IL)-13 is a central mediator of airway inflammation in asthma, and gene polymorphisms may play a role in asthma pathogensis. However, the relationship between IL-13 gene polymorphisms and asthma susceptibility remain unclear. Therefore, we conducted this meta-analysis to evaluate this relationship and better understand the risk of asthma in Chinese children.Methods and ResultsPubMed, cnki.

pmc-12559709.title: Angle-resolved scatterometry combined with deep learning assisted in-situ monitoring of nanowire doping in molecular beam epitaxy process
pmc-12559709.creator: Dekun Yang, Yunfei Song, Wei Liang, Wenze Zhang, Wei Shen, Chong Shen, Kang Liang, Sheng Liu
pmc-12559709.description: The sub-atomic precision of molecular beam epitaxy (MBE) allows for highly flexible elemental doping in nanowires (NWs). Optimizing doping quality for specific elements requires a comprehensive understanding of the relationship between process parameters and doping concentrations. This necessitates in-situ monitoring of the doping process to define the corresponding process window.

pmc-12992670.title: Why Should People with Lived Experience Be Included in the DSM Revision Process?
pmc-12992670.creator: Anne‐Marie Gagné‐Julien, Phoebe Friesen
pmc-12992670.description: Increasingly, scholars and advocates are recognizing the importance of including individuals with lived experience of mental health issues in the development of psychiatric research and policy. Here, we hope to contribute to discussions regarding the specific context of the Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders (DSM) revision process.

pmc-13186029.title: Validation of the Arabic version of the “Cognitive Theory of Mind (ToM-15) scale” among Lebanese patients with schizophrenia☆
pmc-13186029.creator: Maha Bteich, Carole Kassamany, Chadia Haddad, Hala Sacre, Benjamin Calvet, Pascale Salameh
pmc-13186029.description: BackgroundSchizophrenia is characterized by cognitive and social impairments, including deficiencies in Theory of Mind (ToM). Although numerous ToM assessment instruments are available, none have been validated for Lebanese Arabic-speaking individuals with schizophrenia. This study aimed to translate and validate the Arabic version of the Cognitive Theory of Mind Scale (ToM-15).

pmc-13367804.title: Mapping the dialogue: Decoding alveolar stem–niche interactions
pmc-13367804.creator: Ahmad N. Nabhan, Anne Biton, Christine Everett, Conrad Foo, Diana Wu, Joshua D. Webster, Alina A. Alam, Elisa Penna, Sandra Rost, Neha Rohatgi, Rohit Reja, Ranel J. Tulpano, Shiqi Xie, Celine Eidenschenk, Kim Newton, Joseph R. Arron, Vishva M. Dixit
pmc-13367804.description: SignificanceAlveolar Type 2 (AT2) epithelial cells and their surrounding fibroblast niche collaborate to preserve the lung’s gas-exchange surface. When this partnership breaks down, it contributes to lung adenocarcinoma and degenerative lung diseases. We conducted a large-scale, multimodal genetic screen focused on AT2 cell biology.

pmc-13423698.title: Ga-68 FAPI-04 PET/CT detection of repeatedly biopsy-negative poorly differentiated gastric adenocarcinoma: a case report
pmc-13423698.creator: Zhipeng Cheng, Xiuxiu Chang, Yuying Lei, Na Liu, Jing Wu, Lifei Zhang, Aixia Sui
pmc-13423698.description: False-negative endoscopic biopsy may delay the diagnosis of infiltrative gastric cancer, particularly in poorly differentiated or signet-ring cell phenotypes. We report a 56-year-old man with progressive abdominal distension, nausea, vomiting, weight loss, and epigastric pain. Three endoscopic biopsies performed before and after transfer to our hospital showed chronic inflammation without definite malignancy.

pmc-13452867.title: Association between fundus sex index and hypertension, diabetes mellitus, and smoking in the Kumejima study
pmc-13452867.creator: Takehiro Yamashita, Ryo Asaoka, Aiko Iwase, Hiroshi Sakai, Hiroto Terasaki, Taiji Sakamoto, Makoto Araie
pmc-13452867.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). PurposeFundus parameters can be used to quantify masculinity or femininity as a fundus sex index (FSI) ranging from 0 to 1. The purpose of this study was to investigate the association between smoking, hypertension, diabetes, and FSI in the Kumejima population studyStudy designProspective cross-sectional observational population studyMethodsUsing color fundus photographs obtained from the Kumejima population study, 1653 healthy right eyes with reliable fundus parameter measurements were included.

pmc-13548078.title: Visual, visuomotor, and kinesthetic abilities in football players: their relationship with sport-specific performance and trainability
pmc-13548078.creator: Congcong Weng, Dongxu Gao, Xiushen Dong, Yuqing Gao, Qiangquan Wang, Jiayu Wang, Junzhe Zou, Lihao Shan, Honglei Zhang
pmc-13548078.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Success in football (soccer) rests on physical and technical capacity and on the perceptual and sensorimotor systems that let players read the game, act quickly, and control the body and the ball.

pmc-13629319.title: Mapping community-based health promotion strategies for cervical cancer screening uptake: A scoping review of intervention components, delivery models and implementation gaps
pmc-13629319.creator: Nanik Setiyawati, Sri Sulistyowati, Heru Priyanto
pmc-13629319.description: ObjectivesTo map community-based health-promotion strategies used to improve cervical cancer screening uptake and to identify intervention components, delivery models, equity targets and implementation gaps.Study designScoping review.MethodsThe review followed PRISMA-ScR and JBI population–concept–context guidance. PubMed/MEDLINE, PubMed Central, publisher pages, ClinicalTrials.gov-linked records and DOI records were searched from inception through 3 June 2026, with backward and forward citation chasing.

pmc-13632298.title: Prognostic significance and tumor cell interactions of tumor-associated neutrophils in gastric cancer
pmc-13632298.creator: Soo Kyung Nam, Seo Hwan Yu, Sun-Young Ahn, Yujun Park, Hyeon Jeong Oh, Yoonjin Kwak, Seong-Ho Kong, Do Joong Park, Hyuk-Joon Lee, Han-Kwang Yang, Hye Seung Lee
pmc-13632298.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundThis study aimed to determine the clinicopathologic implications and tumor cell interaction of CD66b-positive (CD66b +) tumor-associated neutrophils (TANs) and CD66b and CD177 double positive (CD66b + /CD177 +) activated TANs in gastric cancer (GC).MethodsSingle immunohistochemistry (sIHC) for CD66b, CD8, HER2, p53, and E-cadherin was performed in 1,060 patients with GC, together with microsatellite instability (MSI) testing and Epstein-Barr virus (EBV) in situ hybridization.
